item: U-1 Per-phase capitalised cost shares (Phase I/II/III/preclinical) with disclosed methodology, needed for the capital-channel coefficient c
queries_tried: 1) 'clinical trial cost by phase per patient 2024 2025'; 2) 'Deloitte Measuring the return from pharmaceutical innovation 2025 IRR top 20 biopharma R&D internal rate of return average cost per asset'; 3) 'Eroom's law reversal 2024 2025 R&D productivity return on investment Deloitte pharma IRR new drug approvals per billion dollars trend'; 4) 'clinical trial protocol complexity Tufts CSDD 2024 2025 number of endpoints procedures trial duration trend increasing cycle time phase'
failure_reason: Deloitte's series reports IRR and cost per asset at aggregate level only; the phase-level decomposition sits behind the paywalled full report and behind Tufts CSDD Impact Reports. The DiMasi/Tufts lineage figures that do circulate are the contested capitalised totals, not audited phase shares, and their per-phase splits could not be traced to origin within three hops.
alt_sources_tried: 1) Deloitte 'Measuring the return from pharmaceutical innovation 2025' PDF landing page (aggregate IRR only, no phase split); 2) Tufts CSDD Impact Reports index page (titles only, reports not open access); 3) Drug Discovery Today benchmarking paper on FDA approvals 2006-2022 (reports LoA by company, not cost by phase); 4) BioProcess International and DCAT industry coverage (no phase-level cost tables)
best_estimate: Phase III ~30-40% of capitalised clinical cost; Phase II ~20-25%; Phase I ~10-15%; preclinical+discovery ~15-25%; regulatory review ~3%
best_estimate_basis: Anchored on the one hard sourced datum recovered, Tufts CSDD Phase III conduct cost of $55,716 per day [E-3021], combined with the 9.1-year median clinical span [E-3004] and the standard observation that Phase III is the longest and largest phase. Bounds set wide (+/-10 percentage points on the Phase III share). Effect on this agent's output is confined to capital-channel terms and is roughly +/-30% on those terms; probability-channel elasticities (B1, B2, B8, B10) are unaffected, so the top-3 ranking does not move under either bound.

item: U-2 A published, peer-reviewed elasticity of annual drug approvals with respect to any single pipeline factor
queries_tried: 1) 'clinical trial success rates by phase 2025 probability of success Phase II efficacy failure reasons'; 2) 'Eroom's law reversal 2024 2025 R&D productivity return on investment Deloitte pharma IRR new drug approvals per billion dollars trend'; 3) 'clinical development time trend 2015 2024 median duration first-in-human to approval increasing years oncology cycle time analysis'; 4) 'attrition reasons drug development safety toxicity percentage of failures 2024 analysis clinical trial terminations safety versus efficacy 4 Rs pharma'
failure_reason: No such elasticity appears to have been published. The literature reports levels (success rates, costs, durations) and occasionally first differences, but not partial derivatives of system output with respect to a named factor. This is an absence in the field, not a retrieval failure; the assignment anticipated it and required construction instead.
alt_sources_tried: 1) OECD chapter on Eroom's Law (describes the aggregate productivity trend, offers no factor-level elasticity); 2) Drug Discovery Today benchmarking of 18 companies (LoA levels by firm, no elasticity); 3) Nature Reviews Drug Discovery attrition analysis across four companies (attribution shares, no elasticity); 4) Deloitte innovation-return series (IRR levels and drivers, no elasticity)
best_estimate: All sixteen elasticities in this report are constructed, not retrieved; ranges are 0.0-15% per 10% factor improvement
best_estimate_basis: Constructed with the two-channel model in derived record E-3080 and per-candidate records E-3081 through E-3096, each stating its f, theta, c, tau and delta assumptions explicitly so that Agent R and Agent X can re-derive or contest any single number. Non-additivity and the Amdahl ceiling are logged separately as E-3097 and E-3098 so the ranking cannot be misread as a summable budget.

item: U-3 Modality-resolved share of the active clinical pipeline (cell/gene vs antibody vs ADC vs small molecule vs RNA vs vaccine), needed to weight B6 exactly
queries_tried: 1) 'viral vector CDMO capacity utilization 2025 gene therapy manufacturing bottleneck cost of goods autologous CAR-T manufacturing failure rate'; 2) 'ADC conjugation capacity shortage 2025 fill finish sterile capacity constraint CDMO waitlist bioconjugation slots'; 3) 'gene therapy withdrawn from market 2024 2025 commercial failure reimbursement bluebird Skysona Roctavian uptake payer access cell gene therapy launches'; 4) 'CAR-T manufacturing slot waiting list vein-to-vein time 2024 2025 patients died waiting apheresis capacity constraint'
failure_reason: Pipeline-composition counts by modality are published mainly by subscription trackers (Citeline, Evaluate, GlobalData). The open sources reached give modality counts only within a modality (e.g. 200+ ADCs, 41 in Phase III) and never the denominator of all clinical-stage programs, so a share cannot be computed without assuming the denominator.
alt_sources_tried: 1) BioProcess International / Latham BioPharm viral vector capacity model (batch counts, not program counts); 2) PharmaSource ADC contract manufacturing report (ADC counts only); 3) Oliver Wyman cell and gene therapy commercial landscape (commercial viability, no pipeline denominator); 4) FDA novel drug approvals 2025 page (approvals, not pipeline)
best_estimate: Cell and gene therapy = 10-15% of active clinical-stage programs; ADC = 5-8%; antibody = 20-25%; small molecule = 40-50%; RNA = 5-8%; vaccine = 3-5%
best_estimate_basis: Reconciled from the counts that were recovered: 200+ ADCs in clinical development against a commonly reported total clinical pipeline of the order of 4,000-6,000 programs implies roughly 4-5% for ADC, and cell/gene program counts are consistently reported at roughly twice to three times the ADC count. The B6 system-level elasticity of 0.8-1.8-3.5% was computed at a 12.5% cell/gene weight; substituting 10% gives 1.5% and 15% gives 2.2%, both inside the stated band, so the B6 rank of 9 is stable across the plausible range.

item: U-4 Origin verification for the Tufts CSDD investigative-site productivity figures (48% under-enrolling / 1 in 10 enrolling zero) and the $55,716 per day Phase III conduct cost
queries_tried: 1) 'clinical trial patient recruitment failure rate 2024 sites enroll no patients enrollment bottleneck statistics'; 2) 'number of clinical trials competing for same patients oncology 2025 trial oversupply eligible patient participation rate 5 percent cancer patients enroll'; 3) 'clinical trial protocol complexity Tufts CSDD 2024 2025 number of endpoints procedures trial duration trend increasing cycle time phase'
failure_reason: Both figures are reproduced by multiple secondary aggregators that cite Tufts CSDD without a retrievable primary document. The Tufts CSDD Impact Report series is not open access, so the sample definition (which trials, which years, how a site is counted as activated) could not be confirmed. Under M3 the missing denominator definition caps confidence; under M4 the repeated secondary citation without a reachable primary raises circular-reference risk, and both records are flagged circular_risk true in the ledger for Agent R. STATUS AT STEP 6: partially closed. Agent F reached the same site-productivity conclusions from a non-overlapping source set (0.4 patients per site per month in industry Phase III, halved in four years; 35-61% annual site-staff turnover; unique FDA-regulated investigators -48% from 1999 to 2015), and Agent X added global investigator -9% and coordinator -28% over six years. Five independent restatements now agree and none contradicts. The primary Tufts CSDD Impact Report remains paywalled, so the sample definition is still unconfirmed and the circular_risk flag stays set on E-3020 and E-3021.
alt_sources_tried: 1) Tufts CSDD Impact Reports index at csdd.tufts.edu (titles listed, no full text); 2) Applied Clinical Trials coverage of recruitment bottlenecks (independent restatement, same underlying attribution); 3) Clinical Trial Vanguard conference coverage of Tufts CSDD (independent restatement of the protocol-complexity series, corroborates the source's existence and methodology style); 4) CRIO analysis citing Tufts CSDD for the 2010-2020 cycle-time deltas (fourth independent restatement)
best_estimate: Figures retained as reported: ~48% of activated sites under-enrol or enrol nobody; Phase III conduct ~$55,716 per calendar day (2024)
best_estimate_basis: Four independent secondary restatements agree on both values and none contradicts them, and the oncology-specific figure from a different source (60% of sites enrolling fewer than five, over 20% enrolling none, [E-3022]) is directionally consistent with the 48% figure. That cross-consistency supports retaining the numbers while flagging origin as unverified. B3's elasticity does not hinge on the exact value: dropping the queueing multiplier entirely moves the B3 point estimate from 2.5% to about 1.8%, which leaves its rank of 7 unchanged. At STEP 6 the dependence is smaller still: B3's elasticity was cut to 0.6 on Agent D's model result rather than on these figures, so the ranking no longer turns on them at all.

item: U-5 The pass-through coefficient theta for every probability-channel candidate, and the overlap coefficient rho between B1, B2, B8 and B10
queries_tried: 1) 'clinical trial success rates by phase 2025 probability of success Phase II efficacy failure reasons'; 2) 'attrition reasons drug development safety toxicity percentage of failures 2024 analysis'; 3) 'Phase 2 to Phase 3 dose selection endpoint selection population selection cause of Phase 3 failure percentage analysis clinical development design decisions'; 4) 'Phase 3 oncology failures wrong dose wrong endpoint wrong population analysis proportion avoidable design errors 2024 2025'
failure_reason: No published study estimates what fraction of a named attrition class is removed by a given proportional improvement in the upstream factor, for any factor. The literature attributes failures to causes and stops there. theta is therefore a construction in both this analysis and Agent D's, and rho is explicitly calibrated to my stated band rather than measured - Agent D flags it as the least-supported quantity in its model and I flag it as the least-supported quantity in mine. This is a shared, acknowledged weak point across two independent analyses, not a discrepancy between them.
alt_sources_tried: 1) Nature Reviews Drug Discovery four-company attrition analysis (attribution shares only); 2) Chemical Research in Toxicology 2024 review (attribution shares only); 3) JNCCN empirical Bayes analysis of 362 Phase III oncology trials (error rates, not pass-through); 4) Agent D's model assumptions document section 8, which reaches the same conclusion independently
best_estimate: theta = 0.10-0.45 depending on candidate and observability; rho = 0.60
best_estimate_basis: theta bands are set per candidate on how directly the improvement is observable before the readout that measures it: lowest for B1 (target validity is unverifiable until Phase II reads out), highest for B17 (dose and endpoint choices are observable at the moment they are made). rho = 0.60 is Agent D's calibration to my 11-26% joint band against a 21% naive sum; the resulting 30.5% overcount is stable across both the budget-binding and budget-free cases, which is weak evidence that the coefficient is not doing all the work. Sensitivity: halving every theta halves every probability-channel elasticity proportionally and leaves the ordering of B1, B8, B17 and B2 unchanged, because they share the parameter.

item: U-6 The true improvement-side elasticity of capital (B11) - whether Agent D's zero is real or an artefact of its exogenous-capital assumption
queries_tried: 1) 'biotech venture capital funding 2025 decline clinical stage companies cash runway IRA pill penalty pricing impact on R&D investment'; 2) 'Deloitte Measuring the return from pharmaceutical innovation 2025 IRR top 20 biopharma R&D internal rate of return average cost per asset'; 3) 'Eroom's law reversal 2024 2025 R&D productivity return on investment Deloitte pharma IRR new drug approvals per billion dollars trend'
failure_reason: The two available estimates disagree in a way the evidence cannot presently settle. Agent D's flow model returns zero additional approvals for a 50% budget increase, but D lists capital as exogenous with no feedback from returns onto budget, and tests only a 50% increment - far outside the roughly 11% headroom that exists on the first-binding shared input, so the test cannot distinguish 'capital does nothing' from 'capital saturates a physical cap almost immediately'. Red-team X-10 independently reports abundant deployable capital declining the novel bet, which supports the low estimate from a different direction. No natural experiment isolating a marginal capital increment against fixed physical capacity was found.
alt_sources_tried: 1) Agent D's tornado analysis and scenario set (zero upside at +50%, -46% at -20%); 2) red-team X-10 with about USD 1.3 trillion deployable at the top 25 pharmaceutical companies against novel-target entry falling to about 30 per year; 3) the interrupted time-series on post-IRA trial starts (-11.4 immediate, -1.2 per month), which measures the downside direction only; 4) Deloitte's ex-incretin return series at 2.9%, which measures the return rather than the elasticity
best_estimate: Improvement side 0.0-0.8-3.0 percent per 10% more capital; downside approximately -23 percent of approvals per 10% budget reduction
best_estimate_basis: The asymmetry is the finding and it is better supported than either single number. The downside estimate comes straight from D's tornado (-20% budget gives -46% approvals, elasticity about 2.3) and is corroborated in sign and rough size by the post-IRA interrupted time-series. The improvement-side point of 0.8 is set near D's zero but not at it, because D's exogenous-capital assumption is explicit and because roughly 11% headroom exists on GMP plasmid at u = 0.90 before the first physical cap binds; a 10% increment plausibly fits inside that headroom in a way a 50% increment cannot. The band spans D's zero at the bottom and my original near-linear reading at the top, so a reader who prefers either analysis can read their own answer off the row. B11's rank of 8 is stable anywhere in the band below about 2.6, which covers most of it.
